{{Short description|Japanese geophysicist (1925–2004)}}
'''Syun-iti Akimoto''' (1925–2004) was a Japanese geophysicist. He was described by an [[Eos (magazine)|Eos]] article as a "a pioneer of high-pressure, high-temperature study of the materials of the Earth's deep interior".<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Syono |first=Y. |last2=Yagi |first2=T. |date=2005-11-15 |title=Syun‐iti Akimoto (1925–2004); |url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2005EO460007 |journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union |language=en |volume=86 |issue=46 |pages=465–465 |doi=10.1029/2005EO460007 |issn=0096-3941|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He had the 39th volume of the Geophysical Monograph Series dedicated to his honor.<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1029/GM039 |title=High‐Pressure Research in Mineral Physics: A Volume in Honor of Syun‐iti Akimoto |date=1987 |publisher=American Geophysical Union |isbn=978-0-87590-066-7 |editor-last=Manghnani |editor-first=Murli H. |series=Geophysical Monograph Series |volume=39 |location=Washington, D. C. |language=en |doi=10.1029/gm039 |editor-last2=Syono |editor-first2=Yasuhiko}}</ref> He received a [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] and a [[William Bowie Medal|William Bowie medal]].<ref name=":0" />
